prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability (the fact of the taking) is not contested; the retrial will turn entirely on dollar amounts. Boggess starts the retrial in a weaker evidentiary posture than the first trial because the post-valuation sale/development evidence will come in and the Hempstead-based special-benefits ruling already went against it, meaning UDOT's $2.2 million offset theory will reach the jury largely intact; the ultimate verdict will likely land somewhere between UDOT's offset-heavy position and Boggess's higher severance-damages theory, but I cannot quantify Boggess's net recovery without the underlying land-value and severance-damages figures.

outcome.description: On retrial the jury awarded Boggess approximately $330,000 (the opinion gives only this rounded figure) for the value of the condemned property and found no severance damages, after UDOT's expert was allowed to testify to a $2.2 million project-benefit offset. The Court of Appeals held that interstate access and added travel lanes are general benefits that cannot offset severance damages, found the error harmful, reversed the verdict and remanded for a new trial; no fees are discussed.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed for a new trial; no final figure yet.
